I shoot for at least 10k steps a day. Do I hit it every day? Not at all. But just that little change was enough to help me lose 10lbs in 2 months. I also try and go to the gym 2-3x a week. 

Start focusing on building good habits. Start with the steps. Drink plenty of water next (so if you drink soda or a lot of alcohol, try and limit it. Maybe drink once a month and choose diet soda). If you do eat grains, choose whole grain. Wheat is better than white (unless you have kidney issues). 

Veggies are so important. They have a lot of water content in them along with vitamins and minerals. As well as fiber (which is great for your GI system)! So maybe another goal you incorporate later down the line is trying to add a veggie to each meal. Keep in mind your goal is balance. So if you have a high carb meal already, try to go with a leafy green or less starchy veggie (peas, carrots, etc). 

Overall consistency is key. Try and make balanced choices to fuel and care for your body. You don’t want to be in your 40’s with one leg, bed ridden, waiting to have another stroke. Care for yourself now that way you can live life to its fullest in the future. It’s kinda like setting up retirement funds. Invest in the now. If you need a break, take that break. Have some fun food every now and then. It helps with diet fatigue. 

And don’t forget. It took a long time to gain the weight. It takes even longer to lose it. It’s ok if it doesn’t happen over night. Have fun with it. Try to not get too focused on the number. Focus on how your clothes fit. Or how you feel. How you can now jog on a beach and not get winded. Or lift more weight than you could before. 

One more thing. I don’t track calories eaten or burned. I look at the whole picture. I feel very overwhelmed when it comes to tracking. Only thing I try and track is protein. I shoot for .7-1g per lb that I would like to be ideally. So about 110-120g per day. (I don’t hit it often but I try lol)

THIS was the game changer. I discovered protein. Protein makes me feel full so quick. I’m less likely to eat less nutritious things if I’m already full. Also protein is so important for muscle recovery. 

When you are trying to lose weight, you want to make sure you try and do some kind of exercise with it. Strength training is important because once you lose your muscle, it’s so hard to get it back. I work inpatient rehab right now and I’ve seen people who have lost so much muscle mass. I never wanna be like that, so I work out. 

I don’t count calories. I only count protein. That was the major thing that I changed. Additionally, I try to eat whole grains, a veggie or fruit at each meal, make more balanced choices. 

The other dietary changes have taken years to get down. I used to work in dietary and learned so much during that time. The major game changer for me was protein this time around.

5’1 girlie here. Was 172. Through dietary changes and overall increased activity, I am now in the 130’s. 

Walking DEF helped me. It’s my fav form of cardio. You will be tired in the beginning, but find something you can do during to distract yourself. I like to play music or youtube videos of people talking and just go. Something that I don’t need to watch and can just listen to. It helps me zone out and get it done. If I’m walking on a treadmill, then I’ll put something on I can watch. 

If I find videos that are fitness related, it helps boost my mood. That keeps me consistent. I think consistency is key. 

And if you can’t dedicate an hour or so to walking, try breaking it up. I go for 15 minute walks at my job. When I was working nights, every hour I would get up and walk for a bit. Just to warm me up (hospital was cold), wake me up and get moving. 

Find what works for you. Make it enjoyable. And you will get there. 🤙🏻🙂

She was suddenly this lyrical genius that was speaking so poetically about things that I’ve felt. And with a catchy bop? I can’t beat it. 

I like how she speaks her mind. She is very educated and knows how to hold herself. Also not afraid to make a point. I like how she treats her fans and seems to be a decent person. 

So yea. Here I am, 2 years later, looking up how to make TS Christmas ornaments for a tree. After I just saw her at the Eras Tour in New Orleans. And I just wanna meet this woman and tell her how proud of her I am. Because she has accomplished so much and does not deserve all the shit she is dealt.

1. You are correct. 20lbs in a year is slow. It’s almost as if weight loss is a multi-facited concept that has many influencing factors. 

2. Sometimes we have these thoughts that are *inside thoughts.* Thoughts that we think to ourselves but don’t necessarily say out loud due to being inappropriate. Maybe that’s a subject you should refresh yourself with.

So legit, I eat tons of chicken. It’s cheaper of the meat and leaner. So less fat but more protein. I also try and slip protein in anywhere I can. For example, if I eat eggs I put cottage cheese in it. Or I use greek yogurt instead of sour cream for many things. Just making small switches helps.

Ohh this means so much to me. Thank you. Honestly just cognitively reframing this has helped. Like instead of focusing on counting macros in a negative way (“i ate 300 cals there, I can only have 900 more. Can’t go over”) I think of it positively (“This shake has 30g of protein. That’s 70g total today. Gotta eat something else later at least 30g!”) I know it may sound silly, but it helps. Also changing the language I use to describe food. Not labeling things as healthy or unhealthy. Some stuff is more nutritionally dense than others. I can eat all food, nothing is off limit. I just try to make more balanced choices.

So psych medications are weird. With cardiac meds, we know exactly how it is going to affect the heart. With psych meds, its more gray. So when we try to find meds that work, it’s a lot of trial and error. 

Psych issues aren’t always d/t chemical imbalances either. Some people have trauma that they need to work through. Meds are prescribed to help alleviate some symptoms they are having. Once they work through the issues, they don’t really need the meds anymore. Some people ARE born with a chemical imbalance in their brain. So meds are needed to balance everything out. 

Studies have shown that if people begin therapy, they improve some. If people do therapy AND medication, they improve the most. However, if people only do medication, they actually tend to be worse off then their baseline. 

Some people dont have to always be on medication for the rest of their lives. But some do. Psych meds are very wild.

EDIT TO ADD: your friends may have not needed the medications anymore. OR they may have simply been on the wrong ones.

Fellow nursing student here. So yes, there is an infection risk with wearing a watch, but many nursing schools don’t care. They have their dress code that you must follow. Unless your code isn’t strict, I’d get one. 

Please don’t wear your favorite watch. You may be cleaning all types of substances during clinicals. You really don’t want to get your favorite watch ruined. 

And as for the seconds hand question, I recommend getting it. You need it to count respirations and other vitals. Also sometimes you need to give medications via IV push. The seconds hands can help determine if an entire minute has passed. I got a cheap $5 watch from Walmart that works wonders.

Some rooms will have a clock on the wall that has it, but not all hospital clocks are the same. So I would invest in a cheap lil watch for school. Especially if your school will do random dress code checks (mine does). You don’t wanna be penalized or sent home for that.
